scope: Primary-source research supporting a preliminary documentary review. No code edition below is selected as governing this hospital. Missing evidence is not an established violation or a compliance pass.
edition_policy: Confirm actual site, authority having jurisdiction, permit/design dates, new-versus-existing work, occupancy and clinical uses, adoption instruments, amendments, referenced-standard editions and any healthcare licensure/accreditation/federal obligations before applying enforceable thresholds.

sources.title: Code Adoption Resources
sources.access: Official page indexed excerpt; direct open timed out.
sources.applicability: General explanation of ICC model-code adoption; project adoption unknown.
supported_claims: An authority adopts a designated model code through legislation or regulation incorporating it by reference.
The adopting instrument identifies the edition and should include local amendments.
sources.short_excerpt: The adopting law should state that the designated model code is being adopted with amendments or changes
sources.review_consequence: A recent published code, a donor location, or one IFC coordinate is insufficient to choose the governing edition.

sources.title: Uses of the FGI Codes/Guidelines
sources.applicability: Conditional on adoption or other project obligation; jurisdiction and adopted edition unknown.
supported_claims: FGI says regulatory use should be through adoption by reference; construction must follow the adopted requirements.
sources.short_excerpt: Use of the Guidelines or any portion thereof for regulatory purposes should be accomplished through adoption by reference.
sources.review_consequence: Hospital licensure requirements must be identified independently from general building-code assumptions.

sources.title: Life Safety Code
sources.access: Official page indexed full relevant passage.
sources.applicability: Conditional only: qualifying US Medicare/Medicaid facilities. This hospital's participation, country and applicable dates are unknown.
supported_claims: The cited CMS rule adopted provisions of the 2012 NFPA101 Life Safety Code and 2012 NFPA99 Health Care Facilities Code, with exceptions, effective July5,2016.
CMS identifies 42CFR482.41 as the hospital physical-environment condition.
sources.review_consequence: The newest commercially available NFPA edition cannot simply be substituted for the actual adopted federal requirements.

sources.title: 2023 ASHRAE Handbook Applications, Chapter9: Health Care Facilities
sources.applicability: Explanatory scope of Standard170; specific governing Standard170 edition and adoption unknown.
supported_claims: Standard170 organizes healthcare ventilation requirements by facility and room use, including relative pressure, outdoor ventilation and air exchange, recirculation, filtration, temperature and humidity.
Healthcare facilities may have multiple authorities overseeing construction and operation.
sources.short_excerpt: It provides specific room design requirements for relative air pressure relationships
sources.review_consequence: Room functions/volumes, served-room mappings, airflow and filtration schedules and pressure relationships are prerequisites; duct length alone cannot demonstrate healthcare ventilation compliance.

sources.title: 2018 International Mechanical Code, Chapter6: Duct Systems
sources.access: Official chapter indexed passages; direct open returned403.
sources.applicability: Illustrative model-code requirement only; 2018 IMC not established as governing.
supported_claims: Section603.9 ties duct joint construction to SMACNA/NAIMA standards and requires fastening/sealing; it also specifies listed sealing materials for certain duct products.
sources.short_excerpt: Duct connections to flanges of air distribution system equipment shall be sealed and mechanically fastened.
sources.review_consequence: A cut plan without a specific joint system, construction/pressure class, sealing method and manufacturer details cannot establish permissible fabrication joints.

sources.title: 2018 International Mechanical Code, Chapter12: Hydronic Piping
sources.applicability: Illustrative model-code requirement only; system service and governing edition unknown.
supported_claims: Hydronic fittings must be approved for the installed material and applicable standards; joint preparation and installation requirements depend on joint type.
sources.short_excerpt: Mechanical joints shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.
sources.review_consequence: Pipe length, outer profile and a family name do not authenticate material, wall thickness, joint allowance, pressure/temperature suitability or field preparation.

sources.title: 2021 International Plumbing Code, Chapter6: Water Supply and Distribution
sources.access: Official chapter indexed passages; direct open returned403.
sources.applicability: Illustrative model-code requirements only; 2021 IPC not established as governing. Must distinguish potable distribution, water service, drainage and other fluids.
supported_claims: Water-distribution sizing must use approved methods consistent with accepted engineering practice.
Distribution piping and fittings have material/standard and service requirements, including NSF61 where specified.
Fittings require compatibility/approval for the installed material and specific application; section605.9 prohibits joints using fittings not approved for the installation.
sources.short_excerpt: Methods utilized to determine pipe sizes shall be approved.
sources.review_consequence: No potable-water approval follows from a generic pipe family or a retail price proxy; additional joints need actual material and joint specifications.

sources.title: 2021 International Plumbing Code, Chapter7: Sanitary Drainage
sources.applicability: Illustrative model-code requirements only; gravity service classification and governing edition unknown.
supported_claims: Horizontal drainage requires a minimum slope dependent on applicable conditions; joint requirements depend on the actual piping material.
sources.short_excerpt: Joints shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.
sources.review_consequence: Authored local lengths do not verify flow direction, invert elevations, fixture-unit sizing, slopes, venting or joint suitability.

sources.title: Modifications To Existing Sprinkler Systems
sources.access: Official NFPA educational article indexed passage; direct open returned an empty extraction.
sources.applicability: Publisher guidance on NFPA13 modifications, not itself governing code text. Governing NFPA13 edition and existing approvals unknown.
supported_claims: Modification review needs enough existing plans and design basis for the authority to evaluate the changes.
Hydraulic evidence is needed to substantiate required design flow; the guidance does not assert every modification always requires a complete system recalculation.
Unknown original design basis can require broader analysis.
sources.short_excerpt: A more complex analysis might be required for the entire system if the original design basis cannot be confirmed.
sources.review_consequence: Unchanged line geometry plus added assumed joints is insufficient without water supply, design demand, sprinkler data, pipe and fitting details and hydraulic substantiation.

sources.title: NFPA13: Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems
sources.applicability: Candidate standard family only; edition and adoption unknown.
supported_claims: NFPA13 addresses automatic-sprinkler design, installation and acceptance testing.
sources.review_consequence: Quantity preservation is not acceptance testing or hydraulic/fire-coverage verification.

sources.title: NFPA70 National Electrical Code Development
sources.applicability: Candidate standard family only; edition and adoption unknown. No committee draft is treated as an issued clause.
supported_claims: NFPA70 addresses electrical design, installation and inspection for protection from electrical hazards.
sources.short_excerpt: safe electrical design, installation, and inspection
sources.review_consequence: Conduit/tray lengths alone cannot verify circuits, load/ampacity, protection, grounding/bonding or healthcare essential-power requirements.

sources.publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.title: 29CFR1910.303 General electrical requirements
sources.applicability: Conditional US workplace requirement only; geographic/employer/installation-date applicability unknown. This is not a replacement for the adopted NEC.
supported_claims: Equipment suitability includes size, voltage and current capacity; listed/labeled equipment must follow its associated instructions.
Interrupting ratings must accommodate available fault current; connections and working access have additional requirements.
sources.short_excerpt: Listed or labeled equipment shall be installed and used in accordance with any instructions included in the listing or labeling.
sources.review_consequence: Missing equipment ratings, actual cable data, available fault current and connection details prevent an electrical compliance conclusion.

sources.title: NFPA99 Health Care Facilities Code
sources.access: Official publisher scope summary; current product edition is not selected for this project.
sources.applicability: Candidate standard family only; edition, adoption, clinical risk categories and services unknown.
supported_claims: NFPA99 addresses risk-based healthcare system requirements including electrical and medical gas/vacuum systems.
sources.short_excerpt: risk-based requirements for electrical systems, medical gas and vacuum systems
sources.review_consequence: Medical gas cannot be assumed absent or compliant from generic pipe families; authenticate service and clinical risk before choosing requirements.

sources.title: NFPA72 National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code
sources.access: Official publisher scope summary, which may redirect to a newer product; no edition-specific clause asserted.
sources.applicability: Candidate standard family only; edition and adoption unknown.
supported_claims: NFPA72 covers fire alarm performance, application, installation, inspection, testing and maintenance.
sources.short_excerpt: system performance, application, installation, and ongoing inspection, testing, and maintenance
sources.review_consequence: Device counts without circuit/power/battery, notification, detector coverage and cause-and-effect data cannot verify the alarm system.

research_exclusions: NFPA first-draft, second-draft and public-input committee documents were encountered but not used as enforceable issued clauses.
No Massachusetts, New York, Singapore or New Zealand jurisdiction is inferred from coordinates, donor or host location.
Illustrative code editions do not imply that the hospital was originally designed, permitted or built under them.
No assumed fitting, joint or product is declared prohibited solely because the necessary approval evidence is missing.
